entities.name: Query protein (496 aa)
observations: Sequence length is 496 aa; estimated molecular mass is 49.9 kDa.
Theoretical pI is 5.26 and estimated charge at pH 7 is −14.4, indicating an overall acidic protein.
Sequence is predicted stable by the instability index (23.72) and has near-neutral average hydropathy (GRAVY 0.078).
Strong homologs are reviewed bacterial bifunctional GlmU proteins, with 59.5–60.4% identity, 93.8–94.2% query coverage, and E-values of 1.2e−171 to 3.1e−172.
Homology supports dual activity: glucosamine-1-phosphate N-acetyltransferase and UDP-N-acetylglucosamine diphosphorylase.
Reference GlmU proteins are cytoplasmic homotrimers and bind one Mg2+ per subunit.
Candidate reactions are acetyl-CoA-dependent formation of GlcNAc-1-phosphate and UTP-dependent formation of UDP-GlcNAc.
Pfam scan identifies NTP-transferase-related domains near residues 10–227 and a C-terminal Hexapep-like region around residues 401–435.
Functional evidence is homology-based and should not be treated as direct biochemical validation.

entities.name: GlmU
observations: Bacterial bifunctional enzyme catalyzing the final two steps of UDP-N-acetylglucosamine biosynthesis.
The N-terminal uridyltransferase activity converts GlcNAc-1-phosphate and UTP to UDP-GlcNAc.
The C-terminal acetyltransferase activity converts glucosamine-1-phosphate and acetyl-CoA to GlcNAc-1-phosphate.
Associated with peptidoglycan and, in Gram-negative bacteria, lipid A biosynthesis.
